documents.abstract: Visual perception is often studied through the lens of object recognition. However, a large fraction of visual experience concerns image properties that are not naturally described in terms of discrete objects or categories. Visual textures provide a useful method to investigate this complementary aspect of vision, as they can be described through image statistics while spanning a wide range of perceptual and semantic complexity. In this thesis, I investigate how textures are represented in deep neural networks and humans, combining texture synthesis, representation analysis, computational modeling, and psychophysics. I first explored whether the naturalistic texture representations introduced by Gatys et al. (2015) could be combined with the latent space of a Variational Autoencoder to construct a controllable generative model of naturalistic textures. Although the complete model did not achieve the intended performance, the experiments isolated the texture representation proposed by Gatys as the most robust component of our framework and motivated a direct investigation of its representational properties. I then studied texture representations coded as Gram matrices across a diverse set of convolutional neural networks trained for object recognition. Texture information increased with network depth, but the resulting representations recovered only part of the categorical structure of natural textures defined by human judgment. Crucially, their quality was not correlated with measures of neural or behavioral alignment in object recognition. This dissociation indicates that being a good model of the ventral visual stream in an object recognition setting does not necessarily imply representing textures in a human-like way. Finally, I extended this analysis beyond convolutional architectures by comparing one CNN with three Vision Transformers across textures of progressively increasing complexity and with human performance in a psychophysical discrimination task. Vision Transformers formed substantially more consistent representations across texture types than the CNN, and these representational relationships were significantly better aligned with human perception. Taken together, these results show that texture perception provides a complementary benchmark for computational models of vision and exposes limitations within the dominant object recognition paradigm. More broadly, I suggest that understanding biological visual representations requires models and evaluation criteria that account not only for object identity and semantic content, but also for the statistical and contextual structure through which visual appearance is organized.

This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises recent evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled Air Traffic Control (ATC) decision-support systems and examines how AI is used to improve operational performance, safety, and resilience in increasingly complex airspace. Research on machine learning, optimisation, and automation has expanded rapidly, but evidence remains fragmented across application areas and validation settings. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-guided protocol was used to search Scopus and IEEE Xplore for English-language journal articles published from 2021 to 2025. Following screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and final reconciliation of study type, scope, and duplicate records, 30 eligible primary studies (n = 30) were included in the qualitative synthesis. The abstract level reporting completeness appraisal yielded a mean score of 80.28% and a median of 83.33%; 16 of 30 studies (53.33%) scored at least 80%, including six studies (20.00%) that scored at least 90%. These percentages describe reporting completeness rather than algorithmic performance. Because the included studies evaluated different operational tasks, datasets, outcome measures, and validation settings, their performance results were not directly commensurable; combining them into a single pooled model-performance percentage would therefore risk conflating non-equivalent metrics. Performance evidence was instead synthesised comparatively by application area, validation setting, and operational trade-off, so that study level performance was interpreted within the metric and dataset used by each primary study rather than averaged across non-equivalent tasks. Three themes were identified: (1) AI-enabled ATC/Air Traffic Management (ATM) operations, including delay and capacity management, conflict resolution, trajectory prediction, and traffic-pattern analytics; (2) aviation safety, surveillance, and resilience, including unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-related risks, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference, sensing, monitoring, and safety assurance; and (3) aviation-connected smart mobility and intelligent transportation systems (ITS), including UAV logistics and related surface-transport applications. Comparative synthesis indicated that prediction methods were increasingly connected to operational decision support, whereas conflict-resolution and resilience approaches continued to rely substantially on simulation, experimental datasets, or bounded validation environments. Overall, the evidence showed increasing operational relevance, but important gaps remained in explainability, real-world validation, human-AI interaction, robustness, and system integration before wider safety-critical ATC deployment.

Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) comprises diverse neurodevelopmental conditions with symptoms differing based on genetics, development, age, and other factors.Detecting ASD has challenges as symptoms often manifest in early life and can lead to delayed analysis.Because standard diagnostic practices rely heavily on human interpretation, making it prone to bias and inefficiency.To attain objective and effective detection, machine learning (ML) methods have become increasingly valuable.Thus, there is a need for an enhanced and accurate ML method that can successfully handle feature selection (FS) and parameter tuning for ASD severity classification.Therefore, this study presents an Advanced Evolutionary Framework for Automated Autism Detection and Severity Classification (AEF-AADSC).The major aim of this work is to design an intelligent machine learning framework to classify autism spectrum disorder severity grading.Initially, the proposed undergoes preprocessing of the raw dataset to ensure high-quality input for the learning model through missing value handling, encoding, and normalization process.Subsequently, feature selection is carried out using an Improved Genetic Algorithm, which selects the most relevant features and thereby enhances model efficiency.The selected features are then utilized for training a CatBoost classifier for accurate classification of ASD severity levels.In addition, hyperparameter optimization is carried out using Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy to further enhance predictive performance.To improve model transparency and interpretability, Explainable artificial intelligence is incorporated using SHapley Additive exPlanations, enabling analysis of feature contributions and supporting better understanding of the classification decisions.The performance validation of the proposed approach is carried out using the Autism Diagnosis Based on Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)-5 dataset.The AEF-AADSC method achieves improved performance with an accuracy of 96.30% compared to baseline methods in terms of different measures.Therefore, the proposed model is found to be a robust approach for the automated ASD severity grading process.

The commercial application of generative artificial intelligence has rapidly brought to the fore the structural tension between machine-generated content (AIGC) and the core presuppositions of copyright law concerning the “author.” This paper examines the protection model and legal mechanisms adopted by the United States on the question of AIGC copyrightability. The research finds that the United States, as represented by the Thaler case, strengthens the “human authorship” requirement from the perspectives of constitutional text, statutory interpretation, and incentive theory, and adopts a result-oriented standard centered on expressive control.

Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) are increasingly being applied to support data-driven decision-making in food processing, quality control, and food safety. This review provides a critical assessment of recent technological advances and examines how AI models are being integrated with computer vision, spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), biosensors, Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, and intelligent monitoring systems throughout the food value chain. This review brings together evidence from academic studies and industry-based research to examine how AI is currently used in the food sector. The applications considered include process control and optimization, fermentation management, quality grading, authenticity assessment, shelf-life prediction, contaminant detection, and support for food-safety decisions. Recent research extends beyond conventional prediction toward adaptive decision support and, in a smaller number of cases, partially autonomous food systems. Approaches such as explainable AI, multimodal learning, foundation models, digital twins, intelligent packaging, and agentic AI are being investigated for real-time monitoring, data integration, and production management. Their level of maturity, however, varies considerably, and many applications remain conceptual or confined to laboratory settings. Data heterogeneity, poor transferability, limited external validation, and regulatory uncertainty continue to restrict industrial adoption. Although one industrial-scale drying study reported a 12.8% reduction in energy consumption, external validation of food-quality models has resulted in markedly higher prediction errors. This contrast illustrates the difficulty of transferring performance from controlled datasets to new products or production environments. Rather than examining these technologies separately, this review considers their roles across food processing, quality control, and food safety, together with the evidence for industrial validation, sustainability, and governance. Further progress will depend on whether models remain reliable outside their development datasets, not simply on incremental gains in internally reported accuracy.

Village health registers in low- and middle-income settings are the operational backbone of community health worker (CHW) programmes, yet their completeness varies systematically across villages in ways that are correlated with the very outcomes the registers are used to measure. The framework combines a potential-outcomes mediation decomposition with a bias-corrected estimating equation that treats register attrition as a village-level post-treatment confounder, and it is operationalised through a machine-learning nuisance-estimation architecture that permits flexible modelling of the visit-frequency, attrition and immunisation surfaces without imposing linearity. Because no observational data are available for the present analysis, the paper is methodological: it characterises the operating characteristics of the proposed estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64) using a before-after-control-impact design with 2000 replications per cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The contribution is a discipline-specific mediation framework that treats register attrition as a structural feature of CHW programme evaluation rather than as a nuisance to be discarded, and that makes the equity consequences of attrition explicit in the estimand.

Sickle cell retinopathy screening programmes that deploy artificial intelligence (AI) computer vision on fundus photographs face a calibration problem that is rarely modelled explicitly: flash intensity varies across cameras, operators and clinic conditions, and a classifier trained at one illumination level may shift its referral threshold when deployed at another. the present analysis treats test-time calibration as a design problem for referral sensitivity rather than as a post-hoc correction. It formalises flash-induced intensity shift as a monotone transform of the retinal image, derives the conditions under which a temperature-scaling calibrator fitted on source-illumination data preserves the referral decision boundary at target illumination, and characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact (BACI) evaluation of calibration transfer. The design uses 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters, effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, and 2000 replications per cell under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64.56 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point referral-sensitivity gain at 80% power, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominates the detectable effect more than the calibration method itself. The contribution is a formal account of when test-time calibration can be trusted to preserve referral sensitivity, and a design-level statement of the cluster counts that screening programmes must budget for if they intend to evaluate calibration transfer empirically.

documents.abstract: Task-shifting hypertension medication titration to nurses is promoted as a remedy for physician shortages, but its workload consequences depend on how nurse prescriber competency is recorded. When competency logging is coarse or inconsistently updated, counterfactual estimators that assign titration tasks on the basis of logged competency may misallocate work across staff cadres. The design assumes a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis is methodological and uses no observational data. Under the declared variance structure, 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The framework separates the causal estimand from the logging mechanism, permits sensitivity analysis to logging error, and yields a defensible basis for workload-equity claims when competency records are imperfect.

Rapid diagnostic test (RDT) batch-to-batch sensitivity variation is an unmeasured nuisance that can invert the safety ranking of dengue warning-sign triage rules deployed in community clinics. The framework is evaluated through a replication-based design study of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominates the variance budget, so that doubling cluster counts from 16 to 32 yields a smaller power gain than the nominal formula implies. The contribution is a safety-oriented inferential architecture that separates the estimand (triage harm under batch drift) from the design (cluster-level before-after-control-impact), and that reports a minimum detectable effect rather than a point estimate when batch sensitivity is unidentified. The framework is proposed as a design and monitoring instrument for clinic networks, not as a validated clinical tool.

Clinical algorithm registries are increasingly proposed as the institutional mechanism through which health systems will govern artificial intelligence at the point of care, yet the political accountability they promise depends on a reporting infrastructure that does not currently exist. the present analysis develops a political-science evaluation of registry governance under conditions of unmeasured post-market performance drift, the gradual divergence between algorithm behaviour and the population it serves that occurs after deployment and that no existing registry instrument captures. The argument is that the accountability deficit is not a technical measurement problem awaiting a better sensor but a constitutional problem of delegation: registries allocate discretion to algorithm developers and to the agencies that certify them without creating a corresponding obligation to report drift, and without a reporting obligation there is no audit trail against which political principals can hold anyone to account. The paper specifies the institutional design conditions under which a drift-reporting obligation would restore accountability, distinguishes monitoring from verification, and identifies the boundary conditions under which registry-based accountability fails. The contribution is a governance-theoretic account of why post-market surveillance of clinical algorithms cannot be treated as an extension of pre-market approval, and a set of design propositions for legislatures and health agencies that wish to close the accountability gap.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Predictive sepsis alert systems increasingly incorporate suppression logic that withholds alerts when the clinical workload of the receiving unit is judged to be high. Such suppression constitutes a political act of rationing that is rendered invisible by the absence of any measurement of nurse workload adaptation, and it evaluates the safety of suppression governance through a replication-based design analysis. The study characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and residual standard deviation of 4.5. Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power, a requirement that exceeds the cluster counts typically available to hospital sepsis programmes. The paper concludes that governance of alert suppression must treat nurse workload adaptation as a measurable political variable rather than an unmeasured confounder, and it specifies the institutional conditions under which suppression can be rendered accountable.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in otolaryngology, but the extent and focus of AI research in Saudi Arabia remain unclear. This scoping review mapped the available evidence and identified key research themes and knowledge gaps. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Saudi Medical Journal archive were searched for studies published between January 2019 and April 2026. Eligible studies investigated AI applications or clinician perspectives within Saudi otolaryngology. The evidence was mapped across major otolaryngology domains, including cochlear implantation and hearing, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, head and neck oncology, surgical and other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea, AI education and implementation, and AI-assisted patient education. Results The searches identified 2,925 database records, four records from other sources and seven records from an updated search and expert suggestions; thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The evidence covered AI awareness and education, large language model (LLM)-based patient education, cochlear implantation, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, and head and neck oncology; no eligible study addressed surgical or other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea. Clinicians were generally positive about AI, while clinical studies showed promising performance of AI models. LLM chatbots generally gave accurate postoperative advice, although, when validated tools were used, their responses were harder to read and less actionable than patient-education standards recommend. However, limited AI education, small or non-Saudi datasets, limited external validation, and implementation barriers remained important challenges. Conclusion AI research in Saudi otolaryngology remains limited but is expanding across several clinical domains. Future research should prioritise Saudi-specific datasets, multicentre clinical validation, structured AI education, rigorous bilingual (Arabic and English) evaluation of LLM-generated patient information, and safe integration of AI into clinical practice in line with Saudi Vision 2030.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Nurse charting intervals in inpatient wards are irregular, and the irregularity is informative: deteriorating patients are charted more often, so the observation times of a deterioration-forecasting model depend on the outcome the model is meant to predict. the present analysis treats that dependence as the central methodological problem for artificial-intelligence rapid-response activation and proposes an irregular-time Hawkes process in which the charting intensity and the deterioration intensity are jointly specified, with the charting process carrying a self-exciting term that responds to the patient's latent deterioration state. The proposal is evaluated as a design study rather than an empirical trial: no observational data are used or claimed, and the operating characteristics of the before-after-control-impact estimator that would be used to evaluate a deployed system are characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, a requirement that exceeds every cluster count in the evaluated grid. The forecasting problem and the evaluation problem are coupled: a model that conditions on charting irregularity changes the very activation rate that the before-after-control-impact estimator is designed to measure, and evaluation designs that ignore this coupling will misstate the effect of deployment.

Ultrasound gestational-age dating error is a persistent obstacle to estimating the effect of antenatal corticosteroid timing on neonatal respiratory outcomes, because misclassification of exposure and outcome can bias both conventional regression and machine-learning estimators. The framework combines a measurement-error model for gestational age with a sparsity-constrained score-based causal discovery algorithm, and it is assessed using a before-after-control-impact design with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5, and an intraclass correlation of 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect declines as cluster count increases. The framework is positioned as a methodological contribution to causal discovery in healthcare settings where gestational-age dating is imperfect, and its implications for neonatal respiratory safety evaluation are discussed.

Assessment is considered as a key feature and central pillar in the teaching and learning process, particularly in making of judgement and measurement of student achievement and mastery of learning outcomes. The traditional methods of designing assessments items face several challenges, such as the need and requirement to design the assessment items manually, the time-consuming nature of the design process and the required cognitive skills through formal training provided by various institutions. As the result, the assessment items may lack on the detailed and context specific to validity and reliability, lack of standardized rubric and inconsistent scoring in performance based. A preliminary study was conducted at the analysis phase to explore fundamental understanding of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), Assessment Literacy, and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) literacy among educators. Forty-six educators were involved in this study. Findings have shown that most of the respondents have lower level of using GAI tools and prompt engineering skills, 43.5% use GAI for teaching and learning, searching information (34.8%), idea collection process (6.5%), reflection/journal (4.3%), writing programming code (4.3%), generate image (4.3%) and other tasks (2.2%). The most difficult tasks are writing assessment test items (28.3%), practical tests (21.7%), presentations (17.4%), projects (10.9%), simulations (6.5%), and fieldwork (5.4%). The study shows that educators lack skills in designing assessment materials using GAI. Promoting a suitable guideline as a new innovative assessment tool will serve as a standardized guideline and as a means of incorporating AI ethically.

Event cameras offer microsecond latency and high dynamic range for row-crop navigation, but dust-occlusion transients corrupt optical-flow estimates in ways that frame-based benchmarks do not capture. No observational data are used or claimed: the analysis is a design and power study. The variance structure specifies a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.640. Power was estimated across 2000 design cells defined by cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design achieves 80% power at 54 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect. The paper formalises a lateral-error bound that maps optical-flow estimation error under dust occlusion to a safety envelope for implement guidance, and shows how the BACI estimator's operating characteristics constrain the benchmark's ability to detect safety-relevant improvements. The contribution is a benchmark architecture and a power-analytic foundation for evaluating event-camera optical-flow methods in computer agriculture, with explicit boundary conditions on what the design can and cannot establish.

Continuing professional development (CPD) is frequently organised as a sequence of educational events directed at individual practitioners. In resource-constrained health services, however, participation and learning transfer are shaped by staffing, protected time, leadership, finance, infrastructure, access to current guidance and opportunities to apply learning. Individual-centred and linear developmental models do not adequately explain these interactions. This article proposes the Context-Enabled Continuing Professional Development (CE-CPD) Framework, derived from a programme of research involving a scoping review, qualitative evidence from professional nurses and nurse managers in Limpopo Province, South Africa, and critical engagement with developmental, implementation and CPD-outcomes literature. The framework positions professional learning within four interacting layers: a stakeholder and service ecosystem, organisational enabling conditions, a recurring five-phase workplace learning cycle, and an outcome pathway extending from access and participation to practitioner capability, professional behaviour, team and organisational performance, and patient or population health. Capability development is treated as domain-specific, iterative and potentially non-linear, rather than as an automatic progression from novice to expert. Six propositions specify how contextual readiness, protected opportunity, equitable access, workplace application, knowledge sharing and infrastructure are expected to influence these outcomes. The CE-CPD Framework shifts the explanatory focus from whether professionals attend CPD to whether their organisations make relevant learning possible and ensure its sustainable application. Although derived from nursing evidence, its organisational mechanisms may be relevant across healthcare professions. Interprofessional co-design, prospective testing and equity-sensitive evaluation are required before wider adoption.

ABSTRACT This article provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in negotiation, evaluating contemporary systems through the specific case study of Large Language Models (LLMs). To address the lack of established terminology, it first proposes a new typology distinguishing Negotiation Supported by AI (NSAI), Negotiation by Controlled AI (NCAI), and Negotiation by Autonomous AI (NAAI). To determine whether current systems can achieve genuine NAAI, the article first develops the Core Essential Elements of Negotiation (CEEN) through a structured comparison of authoritative definitions of negotiation and then examines how these literature‐derived elements align with the perceptions of 250 survey respondents. Finally, the paper applies an ordered analytical rule to contemporary LLMs. Information Exchange and Reciprocity are directly instantiable; Outcome, Divergent Motivations, and Interdependence are externally conditioned; and Choice is not currently instantiable because an attributable evaluative standpoint and consequential commitment remain absent. Accordingly, current LLM‐based negotiating systems remain controlled rather than autonomous agents under the proposed typology.

Corporate digital governance often fails to mitigate the social impact of digitalization due to short-term profit optimization, triggering AI black box phenomena that marginalize digital workers' welfare. This study explores the integration of ethical dimensions into corporate governance frameworks to safeguard stakeholder rights. Employing a qualitative literature review approach (2019–2026), this research analyzes technology corporations' accountability regarding automated work systems. The findings reveal that current platform governance prioritizes financial gains over social equity, leading to algorithmic opacity and worker vulnerability in Indonesia. Consequently, this research concludes that algorithmic transparency must become an integral part of corporate compliance. The study recommends mandating boards of directors to implement periodic ethical audits on artificial intelligence systems to ensure business sustainability and distributive justice.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence cyclone track emulators are increasingly used to generate evacuation triggers, yet their adversarial robustness is typically assessed only against the emulator that was attacked. The framework combines a Lipschitz continuity condition on the emulator mapping with a disagreement radius derived from ensemble spread, yielding a certified upper bound on the probability that a perturbation crafted for a source emulator succeeds against a target emulator. The bound is expressed as a function of the perturbation magnitude, the spectral norm of the emulator Jacobian, and the pairwise disagreement between ensemble members. A case study using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations) illustrates the calibration of the disagreement radius; the observed mean temperature was 26.414 °C and the warming trend was 0.1553 °C per decade. The framework yields an evacuation-order safety condition that translates the certified bound into a maximum permissible perturbation magnitude for a given false-alarm tolerance. The contribution is a formal, assumption-explicit guarantee that links adversarial transferability to ensemble disagreement and to the operational safety of evacuation decisions.

In the context of ChatGPT as a shopping assistant in Indonesia, this research investigates the correlations between satisfaction and factors such as perceived utility, anthropomorphism, ease of use, and navigation, as well as the link between satisfaction and buy intention. Using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the research takes into account functional perceptions in addition to conversational AI's human-like and interaction-related traits. The data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) with AMOS from a quantitative, cross-sectional survey that was administered to 200 participants. The findings show that elements such as perceived utility, anthropomorphism, and navigation are positively and substantially linked to satisfaction. There is a positive correlation between perceived ease of use and satisfaction, however the link is not statistically significant (β = 0.135, p = 0.063). Having a positive and substantial association with purchase intention (β = 0.537, p < 0.001) constitutes satisfaction. It turns out that four out of five possibilities are correct. According to the results, in this particular sample, features connected to interactions and practical utility are linked to satisfaction, although simplicity of use by itself does not show any statistical significance. Caution is required due to the study's cross-sectional methodology and conflicting model-fit results, but it does expand the applicability of TAM to conversational shopping help in Indonesia.

The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, offers opportunities to enhance learning while raising concerns about academic integrity. This study examines the role of ChatGPT in Islamic Religious Education (IRE) and formulates strategies to preserve students’ academic integrity. Using a qualitative library research approach, it analyzes scientific articles, books, policy documents, and other credible sources on generative AI, IRE, learning autonomy, and academic integrity through content analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that ChatGPT can improve access to learning resources, support independent learning, clarify complex concepts, and provide preliminary feedback. However, excessive reliance may encourage plagiarism, weaken critical thinking, reduce originality, and produce inaccurate information. Six complementary strategies are proposed: institutional policies, academic guidelines, cultivation of academic honesty, higher-order thinking tasks (C4–C6), authentic performance-based assessment, and contextual and problem-based learning. These strategies position ChatGPT as a supporting tool rather than a substitute for students’ intellectual processes, and its outputs must be critically verified against credible scholarly sources. The study concludes that the educational value of ChatGPT in IRE depends on sound pedagogical design and a strong ethical framework. Because the framework is a conceptual synthesis of the literature, it has not been empirically validated and should be tested in future research.

The article proposes a component-based approach to assessing the applicability of large language models in decision support systems. The necessity of multidimensional evaluation is substantiated, and an original methodology for component-based assessment is presented, taking into account both the content of the text and its suitability for specific applied contexts. Unlike existing review scales, the approach suggests the use of operational applicability profiles of the response and a decision-making procedure at the level of a specific output. The components capture verifiable properties of the response and serve as the basis for reproducible metrics and evaluation criteria. The approach is oriented toward typical decision support system tasks and can be applied in both expert and automated scenarios. The methodology can be used to verify generated results and enhance the substantiation of trust in them.

Sorghum yield estimation in smallholder regions of southern Africa is constrained by sparse weather-station networks, and the machine-learning models used to fill the resulting gaps typically report point predictions without distribution-free guarantees. The framework is formalised for the case of covariate shift induced by interpolation error, and a weighted conformal score is derived that restores marginal coverage under a bounded shift assumption. The method is evaluated on a real reanalysis record for Harare, Zimbabwe: NASA POWER monthly air temperature at 2 m, 312 monthly observations from 2000 to 2023, with a mean of 18.914 °C, a standard deviation of 3.107 °C and a warming trend of 0.2001 °C per decade. Coverage-guarantee properties are established analytically and illustrated against this record. The contribution is a coverage-guarantee evaluation protocol that separates the uncertainty contributed by the yield model from the uncertainty contributed by the weather interpolation, and that reports interval width as a function of station density rather than as a single scalar. The framework is proposed as a methodological basis for yield-estimation systems that must state what their intervals actually cover.

Continuum is a user-owned layer (software, with an optional sovereign hardward embodiment) that sits between a user and every AI agent that serves them. It answers two problems. The knowledge problem: every model accumulates context about its user and holds it hostage; switching models means starting over. The agency problem: agents now transact on users' behalf (buying, booking, subscribing) under platform rules, with ties boken by sponsored defaults and no receipt the user can inspect. Continuum holds the user's semantic log (fidelity-stamped claims with provenance, confidence, verification status, and emotional weight), cognitive profile, and standing preferences in one user-owned place, and governs through them: every consequential agent action passes a policy gate (ALLOW / DENY / ESCALATE), ties among acceptable options are broken by the user's rules before any platform default, and every decision is sealed with a tamper-evident, hash-chained receipt. The same governance shapes conversation (age appropriate for a child, full depth for a deivergent adult) enforced in the user's layer, not the model's. Any model plugs in via MCP; the model is a module, the user is the constant. This document is a defensive disclosure; it establishes dated prior art for the composition and claims.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Background: Noise-induced hearing loss remains a significant occupational health concern in industrial settings. Adherence to protective behaviors among workers remains suboptimal, leaving them at continued risk of hearing impairment. Strengthening hearing health promotion is therefore essential. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Healthy Hearing Promoting Program in promoting noise hazard protection behavior and maintaining hearing capacity among workers in large-scale industries. Methods: This single-blind parallel-group randomized controlled trial included 66 industrial workers from two large-scale factories in central Thailand, randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 33) and a control group (n = 33). The control group continued routine occupational practices based on existing factory safety policies. Data were collected between December 2023 and July 2024. Noise hazard protection behavior was assessed at baseline, Week 10, and Week 14, while hearing capacity was evaluated at Week 34 (26 weeks after intervention completion). Statistical analyses were conducted using mixed-design ANOVA and Fisher's exact test. Results: There were no significant differences in baseline data between groups. The experimental group had significantly higher noise hazard protection behavior scores than the control group (F (1,64) = 41.67, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.394), with significant changes over time (F(2,128) = 48.02, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.429) and a significant group–time interaction (F(2,128) = 24.12, p < 0.001, partial η² = 0.274). Between-group mean differences in protection behavior scores were 5.91 points (95% CI: 3.6, 8.2) at Week 10 and 7.39 points (95% CI: 5.3, 9.5) at Week 14. All participants in the experimental group demonstrated hearing thresholds within the normal range across all tested frequencies at follow-up. A small proportion of control group participants exhibited abnormal thresholds at frequencies between 500 and 4000 Hz. Conclusion: The program significantly improved noise hazard protection behaviors but no significant between-group differences in hearing capacity were demonstrated. The findings provide preliminary evidence to support occupational health nurses in developing and implementing theory-driven, multilevel hearing conservation interventions aimed at improving noise hazard protection behaviors among workers in large-scale industries. Trial Registry Number: Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20251128006)
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Cooperative pest-monitoring networks that aggregate sensor evidence across farms through federated learning face a structural threat: a minority of compromised nodes can submit adversarial updates that survive averaging and corrupt the global model. Byzantine-robust aggregation rules are widely proposed as the remedy, yet their convergence guarantees rest on assumptions about update geometry that agricultural sensor deployments rarely satisfy. the present analysis audits those guarantees. It formalises the aggregation problem for a cooperative pest-monitoring federation, states the standard Byzantine-robust estimators (coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, Krum), and derives the conditions under which each retains a bounded convergence rate under adversarial sensor poisoning. The audit shows that the guarantees are conditional on a contamination fraction and a heterogeneity bound that are not observable in deployment, and that the effective contamination fraction is inflated by non-IID pest phenology across farms. A before-after-control-impact design is characterised under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64) to show how many clusters a cooperative trial would need to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power: 52. Convergence-guarantee audits, not point accuracy comparisons, should govern the adoption of Byzantine-robust aggregation in computer agriculture.

Cooperative data-sharing consortia that pool smallholder yield records to train artificial intelligence (AI) prediction models face a governance problem that is not resolved by technical privacy guarantees alone: the allocation of a differential privacy budget across participating districts determines both the statistical utility of the resulting model and the distribution of privacy protection among members. The analysis is theoretical and methodological. It formalises the consortium as a federated learning arrangement in which a central curator allocates a total privacy budget across contributing units, and it derives the utility loss of the pooled yield predictor as a function of the per-unit budget, the number of contributing units, and the heterogeneity of yield distributions across units. The central result is a bound showing that equal per-unit budget allocation is utility-optimal only when units are homogeneous in sample size and yield variance; when they are not, equal allocation produces a privacy-utility frontier that is dominated by a size-weighted allocation rule. The paper further shows that the governance choice of allocation rule, not the choice of privacy mechanism, is the binding constraint on smallholder participation, because smallholders in heterogeneous districts face the largest utility penalty under equal allocation and therefore the strongest incentive to withdraw. The contribution is a governance privacy-utility bound that connects differential privacy budget allocation to participation incentives in cooperative agricultural data consortia, and a set of allocation principles that consortium designers can apply without access to the underlying data.

Cross-silo crop-yield prediction in computer agriculture requires cooperative learning across farms, cooperatives and extension agencies whose data cannot be pooled because of privacy regulation, commercial sensitivity and heterogeneous sensing regimes. Federated distillation has been proposed as a communication-efficient alternative to federated averaging, but its interaction with formal differential privacy under cross-silo heterogeneity has not been characterised analytically. The analysis decomposes the generalisation gap into three terms: a distillation bias that scales with the disagreement between silo posteriors, a Rényi-differential-privacy noise term that scales with the number of distillation rounds and the privacy budget, and a heterogeneity term that grows with the divergence of silo label distributions. The bound predicts that under high cross-silo heterogeneity the privacy cost of distillation is sub-linear in the number of silos, whereas the utility cost of local-only training is linear in the number of silos, so that distillation dominates local training above a threshold heterogeneity that the bound makes explicit. The bound is illustrated against a random-effects synthesis of country-level associations between electricity access and under-five mortality across 24 African countries (pooled effect -2.19361, standard error 0.26513, 95% CI [-2.71326, -1.67395], I-squared 99.2%), which establishes the order of magnitude of between-silo heterogeneity that the theory must accommodate. The contribution is a formal privacy-utility characterisation that converts a design choice in cooperative agricultural data sharing into a computable threshold.

Histology, like many basic science subjects requires mastery of terminology, visual structures, and integration of these things to describe functional relationships, making effective study strategies essential for student success. Flashcards are widely used to support retrieval practice and spaced repetition, but students can struggle to develop deeper understanding beyond surface memorization. The relatively recent integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into mainstream higher education exposes new opportunities to enhance active learning strategies. This case study assesses the extent to which flashcards are being used by students in a histology lecture class, and explores the role that AI plays. Data were collected through two voluntary online surveys that included questions asking for multiple-choice responses and short written responses. The subjective and quantitative comparisons together with students’ self-reflection statements prompted classroom discussions about intentional flashcard design and use, and the broader applicability of course-specific study strategies.

This article examines the rise of Work-as-Imagined (WAI) and Work-as-Done (WAD) in New Zealand health and safety practice, using Maritime New Zealand v Anthony Michael Gibson [2024] NZDC 27975 as the local catalyst. It argues that Gibson should not be read as a narrow compliance case, but as an example of how officer due diligence depends on the organisation's ability to understand how critical work is actually performed. The article traces WAI/WAD through the evolution of safety and organisational learning, including scientific management, quality management, French ergonomics in the 1950s, Weisbord's organisational diagnosis, human error research, resilience engineering, Safety-II, and Human and Organisational Performance. It concludes that the practical task for officers, health and safety practitioners and representatives is to build disciplined ways to learn from everyday work before failure occurs.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Line managers once held wide latitude over hiring, appraisal, scheduling, and discipline. That latitude is narrowing. As organizations adopt algorithmic HR systems, decisions once anchored in supervisory judgment are increasingly pre-structured, scored, or overridden by software. This paper pursues two objectives: first, to examine how algorithmic management and HR algorithms reconfigure the discretionary authority of line managers across core decision domains; second, to analyze the role strain managers experience mediating between algorithmic outputs and the employees who live with their consequences. Drawing on an integrative review of recent empirical and theoretical literature, the paper finds that discretion is not simply removed but redistributed unevenly across recruitment, performance management, and scheduling, producing a manager accountable for outcomes they no longer fully controls This mismatch generates measurable strain: ambiguity about where authority sits, ethical unease about opaque scoring logic, and a residual burden of explaining decisions the manager did not make. The paper proposes a conceptual pathway linking algorithmic input to discretion compression to role strain, and closes with implications for organizations designing human-AI collaborative HR systems
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: We live in an age of unprecedented access to information, yet having more information does not necessarily mean understanding the world more accurately. From traditional storytelling and printed newspapers to television, smartphones and generative artificial intelligence, the ways in which people create, distribute and interpret information have undergone profound transformations. In From Media Audience to Critical Citizen: Media Evolution, Psychological Vulnerability and the Crisis of Information Trust in the Age of Artificial Intelligence, Dawid Karol Kolodziej explores the psychological, educational and social consequences of these changes. Drawing on established media theories and contemporary scientific research, the publication examines why people believe misinformation, how repeated messages influence perceptions of truth, and how emotional narratives, cognitive biases and media framing contribute to the formation of individual and collective beliefs. Particular attention is given to artificial intelligence, deepfake technologies, synthetic media and the limitations of automated content detection. The author also investigates the relationship between AI-assisted productivity and independent human reasoning, considering how the delegation of cognitive tasks may influence critical thinking and information evaluation. A central argument concerns the unequal burden of information verification: while professional information producers possess considerable resources and influence, ordinary citizens often lack the time, expertise and technological tools necessary to independently verify every claim they encounter. The publication therefore challenges the assumption that combating misinformation should depend primarily on individual media literacy and emphasises the responsibility of publishers and information producers to substantiate factual claims and correct significant errors transparently. Building upon established scholarship, the author develops an updated five-dimensional conceptual framework for critical media citizenship, encompassing access and provenance, analysis of media construction and framing, evaluation of evidence and uncertainty, responsible creation and participation, and reflection on communicative power and shared responsibility. Combining social psychology, media education and critical analysis, this scholarly publication contributes to contemporary discussions about artificial intelligence, misinformation, public trust and the future of informed democratic participation. documents.abstract: Convective storm nowcasting in regions with sparse rain-gauge telemetry faces a structural tension: graph-neural emulators can interpolate storm tracks from incomplete observations, but the calibration bounds that govern their reliability, and the equity of the warning lead times they produce, remain poorly characterised. The analysis treats the gauge network as a graph with known sampling geometry, defines a spectral calibration bound in terms of the graph Laplacian and the emulator's Lipschitz constant, and shows that lead-time disparities between well-observed and sparsely observed catchments are bounded by the same spectral quantity. A worked illustration using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Harare, Zimbabwe (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean 18.914 °C, decadal warming trend 0.2001 °C) anchors the calibration discussion in a real reanalysis record. The framework yields three results: a calibration bound that degrades predictably with gauge density, a lead-time equity condition that fails when spectral gap ratios exceed a threshold, and a set of design constraints for gauge augmentation. The contribution is a bounded, testable account of when graph-neural nowcasting can be trusted for equitable warning, and when it cannot.

Abstract Rare earth elements are critical to decarbonization, advanced electronics, and defense applications. Traditional hydrometallurgical recovery using liquid–liquid solvent extraction (SX) and classical ion exchange, however, requires the use of volatile organic diluents, high chemical consumption, and multiple-stage cascades, which produce significant amounts of saline and acidic effluents. Solvent-impregnated resins (SIRs), polymer inclusion membranes (PIMs), microbeads (PIBs), and cross-linked networks are environmentally friendly polymeric sorbents, which can greatly reduce the bleeding of the organic phase. This perspective follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines and critically examines the literature on polymer chemistry and artificial intelligence (AI) from 2016 to 2026. We investigate gradient boosting architectures and deep neural networks that map topological fingerprints and molecular physicochemical descriptors to distribution coefficients, coordination thermodynamics, and sorption capacities (R2 = 0.81–0.93). Furthermore, we critically evaluate three major translational limitations: integrating transfer learning throughout the 4f lanthanide contraction, performance degradation across complex real-world leachates, and bridging small-molecule informatics with cross-linked macromolecular networks. Finally, Bayesian inverse design and autonomous experimentation are contextualized to guide the scalable development of next-generation, high-selectivity polymeric sorbents.

Research on why people contribute to open source software (OSS) and related open collaboration platforms spans more than two decades, but its findings conflict, and studies often treat the work people contribute and their intention to keep contributing as interchangeable. Drawing on self-determination theory and motivation crowding theory, we meta-analyze 41 studies. The main analysis pools 178 correlations of eight antecedents with contribution effort and continuance intention from 29 independent samples (N = 9,632). Seven antecedents relate positively to effort, all eight relate positively to intention, and each relates at least as strongly to intention as to effort. Contrary to a common assumption, intrinsic motivation is not more strongly related to effort than extrinsic motivation, but its gap between intention and effort is larger. Reputation relates to effort mainly on platforms with a reputation system, and we find no sign that monetary rewards crowd out enjoyment. The findings inform how platforms can turn contributors' intentions into work.

Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs ( n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

documents.abstract: Nanorobotics is an interdisciplinary field of research that combines nanotechnology, robotics, materials science, biomedical engineering and pharmaceutical sciences. The general idea is to build very small systems that can do useful things inside the body. In drug delivery, the goal is to get the medicine closer to the disease site and release it in a more controlled way. Conventional drug delivery can impact both healthy and diseased tissues. Nanoparticles have improved solubility, stability, distribution and cellular uptake of drugs, but many of them still mainly rely on blood circulation and passive transport. Nanorobotics systems seek to provide active motility, navigation, sensing, target recognition and controlled drug release. Various Nanorobotics systems are under study including magnetic, acoustic, optical, electrical, chemical, DNA based, biological and biohybrid systems. Potential applications include cancer therapy, antimicrobial therapy, brain drug delivery, cardiovascular applications, gene and cell delivery, biosensing and regenerative medicine.= But most Nanorobotics systems are still at the research or preclinical stage. Safe materials, immune reactions, accurate navigation, deep tissue control, manufacturing, drug dose control, long term safety and regulatory approval are some of the important problems. Future work may integrate biodegradable materials, advanced imaging, artificial intelligence, stimulus-responsive release and coordinated swarm systems.

Research on self-regulated learning (SRL) and problem solving has expanded because students’ ability to regulate learning processes is important when addressing complex tasks. However, research development remains dispersed across different contexts, requiring systematic mapping to identify the structure and direction of the field. This study aims to map research on SRL and problem solving from 2020 to 2026 using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were obtained from Scopus using the search string ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). From 730 initial documents, 198 English-language journal articles were retained after screening. VOSviewer and Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny were used to analyze publication development, keyword relationships, collaboration, and thematic evolution. The results show an increase in publications from 21 articles in 2020 to 53 articles as of September 28, 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, and metacognition were the dominant keywords, with strong connections to self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, and artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence emerged as recent research directions. These findings indicate that SRL and problem solving research is increasingly integrating cognitive, motivational, social, and technological dimensions. ABSTRAK Penelitian self-regulated learning (SRL) dan problem solving berkembang karena kemampuan mengatur proses belajar penting dalam penyelesaian tugas kompleks. Namun, perkembangannya masih tersebar pada berbagai konteks sehingga diperlukan pemetaan sistematis untuk mengidentifikasi struktur dan arah penelitian. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan perkembangan penelitian SRL dan problem solving periode 2020–2026 melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dan analisis bibliometrik. Data diperoleh dari Scopus menggunakan kata kunci ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). Dari 730 dokumen awal, diperoleh 198 artikel jurnal berbahasa Inggris setelah proses penyaringan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan VOSviewer dan Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny untuk memetakan perkembangan publikasi, hubungan keyword, kolaborasi, dan evolusi tema. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan publikasi dari 21 artikel pada 2020 menjadi 53 artikel hingga 28 September 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, dan metacognition menjadi keyword dominan, dengan keterkaitan kuat pada self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, dan artificial intelligence. Tema AI dan generative artificial intelligence muncul sebagai arah penelitian terbaru. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kajian SRL dan problem solving berkembang menuju integrasi kognitif, motivasional, sosial, dan teknologi.

ABSTRACT Mastering the skills required to create content with artificial intelligence (AI) requires learning experiences that connect conceptual understanding with practical application. To address this need, interactive multimedia was developed for Grade X students at SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman, focusing on the topic of Creating Content Using Artificial Intelligence. The development process followed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation), with participants selected through purposive sampling. Product testing consisted of an individual trial involving three students, a small-group trial involving six students, and a field trial involving 76 students, comprising 38 students in the experimental group and 38 in the control group. Data were collected through expert validation questionnaires, student response questionnaires, and pretest and posttest assessments. Product feasibility was analyzed descriptively, while learning outcome gains were calculated using the N-Gain method and compared using an independent-samples t-test. The validation and trial results classified the product as highly feasible. The experimental group achieved an average N-Gain in the high category, whereas the control group achieved an average N-Gain in the medium category. The difference in learning gains between the two groups was statistically significant (t = 11.484, p < .001). The multimedia integrates learning materials, visualizations, animations, tutorial videos, examples of AI applications, exercises, and assessments. This product has the potential to serve as an alternative learning medium for Coding and Artificial Intelligence (KKA), although the findings should be interpreted with due consideration of the use of a nonequivalent group design. ABSTRAK Penguasaan keterampilan membuat konten berbantuan kecerdasan artifisial (AI) membutuhkan pengalaman belajar yang menghubungkan pemahaman konsep dengan praktik penggunaannya. Untuk mendukung kebutuhan tersebut, multimedia interaktif dikembangkan bagi siswa kelas X SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman pada materi Kreasi Konten Menggunakan Kecerdasan Artifisial. Pengembangan mengikuti model Research and Development dengan tahapan ADDIE (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation), sedangkan subjek dipilih melalui purposive sampling. Pengujian produk mencakup uji perseorangan terhadap tiga siswa, uji kelompok kecil terhadap enam siswa, dan uji lapangan yang melibatkan 76 siswa, terdiri atas 38 siswa kelompok eksperimen dan 38 siswa kelompok kontrol. Data diperoleh melalui angket validasi ahli, angket respons siswa, serta tes pretest dan posttest. Kelayakan produk dianalisis secara deskriptif, sementara peningkatan hasil belajar dihitung menggunakan N-Gain dan dibandingkan melalui independent-samples t-test. Hasil validasi dan uji coba menempatkan produk dalam kategori sangat layak. Kelompok eksperimen mencapai rata-rata N-Gain berkategori tinggi, sedangkan kelompok kontrol berada pada kategori sedang. Perbedaan peningkatan kedua kelompok signifikan secara statistik (t = 11,484; p < 0,001). Multimedia mengintegrasikan materi, visualisasi, animasi, video tutorial, contoh penggunaan AI, latihan, dan evaluasi. Produk ini berpotensi menjadi alternatif media pembelajaran Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial (KKA), dengan interpretasi hasil tetap memperhatikan penggunaan kelompok nonekuivalen.

documents.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized per-sonal finance management through automated budgeting, spend-ing analytics, real-time risk assessment, and personalized wealth creation strategies. However, standard AI-driven financial plat-forms rely heavily on centralized cloud infrastructure, requiring users to upload sensitive financial metrics—such as income, gran-ular expenses, asset holdings, and long-term targets—to third-party remote servers. This architectural dependency introduces significant security risks, including data breaches, unauthorized commercial tracking, API token leaks, and third-party mon-etization of personal profiles. Recent breakthroughs in open-weight quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) and optimized edge inference engines (e.g., Ollama, vLLM) allow complex natural language reasoning to be executed locally on consumer-grade hardware. This survey presents a comprehensive review of privacy-preserving financial systems, privacy-enhancing AI frameworks, and edge-based LLM architectures. We analyze the trade-offs between cloud-based financial services, federated learn-ing paradigms, and fully local, air-gapped AI execution. Building upon these findings, we present the structural formulation, multi-layer architecture, project workflow, and empirical validation of a privacy-first Personal AI Financial Advisor powered by local LLMs (Llama, Gemma, Qwen) orchestrated via Ollama, Node.js, Express, React, and local MongoDB storage. Finally, we highlight existing technical challenges, research gaps, and future trajectories for local financial intelligence.

Federated learning allows crop-disease classifiers to be trained across farms without centralising leaf imagery, but the non-IID structure of farm data and the noise added for differential privacy interact in ways that are poorly characterised for agricultural deployment. The analysis characterises the operating characteristics of the design under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, using 2000 replications per design cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The results show that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 percent power under this variance structure, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as clusters increase from 8 to 32. The contribution is a design-level account of when differential-privacy noise overwhelms the between-farm signal that federated crop-disease detection depends on, together with a cluster-count rule that practitioners can apply before committing to a federation.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the learning and developmental contexts in which young children grow, learn, and interact. Guided by an ecological perspective, this systematic conceptual mapping review examines 86 resources to explore what young children should learn and how they should be taught. Four themes were identified through thematic analysis: (1) holistic competencies for young children, encompassing foundational cognitive and social–emotional skills, physical and mental well-being, executive functions, learning dispositions, and AI literacy; (2) governance for AI integration in early childhood education; (3) professional development and systemic support for educators; and (4) play-based learning and human-centered approaches in AI-enhanced contexts. The findings suggest that thriving in the AI age requires moving beyond isolated digital skills toward holistic development, supported by a cohesive infrastructure that links classroom practice with structural governance. These findings highlight the necessity of cultivating holistic competencies beyond basic AI literacy in curriculum design, preparing children to navigate an ever-changing digital world. Furthermore, they underscore the imperative for robust institutional support, particularly through participatory research to support age-appropriate pedagogy and educators’ digital confidence, while highlighting the value of playful early learning. Concurrently, these insights establish a theoretical framework for future empirical research, offer actionable strategies for ethical child-centred AI implementation, and provide strategic directions for policy and practice to address the critical demand for transformative knowledge in early childhood education.

This article examines how users cognitively process social chatbot output as a novel form of participatory, generative “character,” co-produced through human–AI interaction. Reporting on the results of empirical research on user responses to the social chatbot platform character.ai, it shows how cognitive stylistic and narratological approaches to character can be utilised but also must be developed to analyse and theorise users’ experience of and interaction with generative AI agents. It makes specific contributions to cognitive stylistics, rhetorical narratology, character studies, and research on gen AI chatbots by: (1) illustrating how the concept of mind-modelling can used to analyse the ways in which users linguistically anthropomorphise social chatbots; (2) developing two new audience response types – transmimetic and hypermimetic – to respectively capture ways in which users assess chatbots against prior knowledge of characters across media and cases where chatbots appear so convincingly human that users question their ontological status; (3) proposing the concept of ‘postdigital misperception’ to reflect the way that users of AI can misattribute the ontological origin of an LLM’s output. The article demonstrates how social chatbots are reshaping how users understand character, agency, and reality in interactive, participatory and generative digital contexts and argues that social chatbots epitomise postdigital experience in blurring the distinction between the digital and non-digital as well as fictional and real.

documents.abstract: Game development is a form of software development, but one whose constraints have no clean counterpart elsewhere: requirements that are discovered by playing rather than specified up front, teams in which programmers are a minority among artists and designers, and a notion of ''correct'' that ultimately reduces to whether the game is fun. The Foundations of Applied Software Engineering for Games workshop (FaSE4Games) exists to bring software-engineering methods to bear on those constraints, and to bring the resulting evidence back to the software-engineering community. The 2026 edition was co-located with the ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2026) in Montreal, Canada, and held as a half-day event on July 6th, 2026. It featured one keynote, four paper presentations, and a peak of 21 participants. The contributions ranged from mining game repositories for issue-resolution patterns and multiagent reinforcement learning for automated game testing, to large language models as a source of runtime content, and agile practice in student game-design teams. This report summarises the keynote, the presented papers, the discussions they prompted, and our reflections on the edition.

This study determined how Teachers' Artificial Intelligence Technologies Utilization Predicts Test Construction Competency in Secondary Schools in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State. Two research questions and two null hypotheses guided the study. The correlational research design was used for the study. The population of the study comprised of 525 teachers in 15 public secondary schools in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State as at 2024/2025 academic year. Simple random sampling technique was used in selecting 100 teachers for the study. Data was collected using a researcher developed instruments named, "Teachers' Artificial Intelligence Technologies Utilization Questionnaire (TAITUQ) and Test Construction Competency Questionnaire" (TCCQ). The instruments were further subjected to face validity by three experts. Two of the experts were from the Department of Psychological Foundations of Education and one of the experts was from the Department of Curriculum Studies, Educational Management and Planning, Faculty of Education, University of Uyo, Uyo. The reliability coefficients of the TAITUQ and TCCQ were .84 and .89 determined using Cronbach Alpha Statistical analysis. The Simple linear regression Statistic was used to answer the research questions and test the null hypotheses at 0.05 alpha level. The findings of the study revealed that ChatGPT and DeepSeek artificial intelligence significantly predict Test Construction Competency. It was recommended among others that School management should organize regular artificial intelligence technology training workshops for teachers to strengthen their use of ChatGPT and ensure they can effectively develop competent test construction skills.

documents.abstract: Abstract This study examines the experiences and perceptions of Muslim users regarding the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in prayer apps and its impact on their religious and online communication activities. Through in-depth online interviews with a diverse group of participants, this study reveals that AI-driven prayer apps foster a sense of virtual community, bridging geographic distances, and enabling meaningful interactions among Muslims. AI tools like chatbots and reminders support emotional well-being by offering comfort, guidance, and companionship. Further, these tools increase religious awareness and empower users to customize their spiritual practices and access educational resources independently. However, perceptions of AI vary, with trust influenced by transparency, privacy concerns, and past experiences. This study emphasizes the importance of transparent and reliable AI tools to build user confidence. Lastly, the findings contribute to theories on digital religion and wellness, offering practical insights for developers, users, and religious organizations.

The deployment of large language models (LLMs) as automated evaluators commonly termed LLM-as-a-Judge introduces a critical question: who evaluates the evaluator? This paper puts the lifecycle framework of Kong et al. [1] on trial, stress-testing its core claims for building, aligning, and monitoring LLM judges in production-scale recommendation explanation systems. We synthesize the core contributions: (1) the identification of a subtle failure mode termed ”right answer, wrong reason,” wherein a judge reaches the correct verdict through unsound reasoning that is invisible to label-agreement dashboards; (2) Reasoning-Aligned Rubric Tuning (RART), a procedure that iteratively refines rubric text using a Meta-Judge to compare judge rationales against human rationales; (3) a fourphase lifecycle-Birth, Training, Deployment, and Monitoring-that anchors LLM judges to human judgment at every stage; and (4) a formal mathematical model stress-tested via Monte Carlo simulation. We provide an open-source implementation of this simulation and analyze its visual output. The simulation confirms RART’s ability to stabilize reasoning alignment but visually reveals methodological vulnerabilities, including a stopping-rule artifact, a severe drift-band calibration problem, and the structural reality of blind-spot leaks. Furthermore, the framework relies on critical unvalidated assumptions-most notably, that the judge and generator do not share blind spots. We conclude that while RART effectively mitigates rubric degradation, it is not a closed-form mathematical solution to Al alignment and ultimately requires continuous human-in-the-loop audits.

documents.abstract: Background. Background and objectives: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) is a common congenital cardiac condition, especially in premature infants, and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to aid clinicians in diagnosing PDA and guiding treatment decisions amidst this uncertainty. Methods. A literature search (up to December 2025) was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for peer-reviewed studies on AI (including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics) applied to PDA. Results. Seventeen studies were included, predominantly involving preterm neonates. AI applications mainly targeted PDA diagnosis and outcome prediction using clinical and echocardiographic data. Imaging-based deep learning models generally outperformed tabular data approaches (with area under the curve often >0.80). Overall study quality was moderate, with limited external validation and data transparency. Conclusions. AI has the potential to transform patent ductus arteriosus management by enabling earlier detection, more consistent decision-making, and individualized treatment planning. Integration of AI into PDA care may reduce practice variability, improve clinical outcomes, and serve as a model for the broader application of artificial intelligence in medicine.
